question: What is the main focus of a community diagnosis?

options.A: The administrative duties of senior doctors
options.B: The recovery rate of a single patient
options.C: The financial budget of a local hospital
options.D: The health status of a whole population

explanation: A community diagnosis looks broadly at the health and living conditions of an entire community rather than focusing on one individual patient. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why must community members be involved in a community diagnosis?

options.A: To reduce the workload of the local government entirely
options.B: To ensure health programs fit their local culture and needs
options.C: To provide financial funding for hospital construction
options.D: To train as professional medical doctors in the village

explanation: Involving the community helps nurses understand local beliefs and realities, making health interventions much more acceptable and successful. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h1)

question: The main reason for establishing baseline data during a community diagnosis is to:

options.A: Punish health workers who fail to meet their targets
options.B: Have a reference point to measure future health changes
options.C: Stop community members from asking for more clinics
options.D: Increase the cost of buying essential clinic drugs

explanation: Baseline data gives nurses a starting measurement so they can later check if their health programs are actually making a difference. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h2)

question: Why is uncovering hidden health needs an important goal of community diagnosis?

options.A: Doctors refuse to treat patients who walk into the clinic
options.B: Hospital records always contain complete and flawless data
options.C: Many sick people stay at home and never visit a health facility
options.D: Government officials order nurses to hide serious diseases

explanation: Hospital registries only capture those who manage to reach the clinic, leaving out vulnerable people suffering in silence at home. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h2)

question: How does community diagnosis help prevent the waste of medical resources?

options.A: By stopping people from falling sick during the rainy season
options.B: By removing the need for any community health workers
options.C: By allowing nurses to keep extra drugs in their private homes
options.D: By pointing out the exact problems that require urgent attention

explanation: Clear data ensures that limited funds and supplies are spent on solving real community problems rather than guessed priorities. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h3)

question: A clinic has funds to build either a new youth center or a borehole for clean water. A community diagnosis shows high rates of waterborne diseases. What should be funded first?

options.A: Both projects equally, regardless of the community health data
options.B: The youth center, because young people complain the loudest
options.C: Neither project, until the national government gives more money
options.D: The borehole, because it addresses the identified health crisis

explanation: Resources must be directed toward solving the specific health threats uncovered during the diagnostic assessment. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h3)

question: What is the main benefit of involving local residents in data collection?

options.A: It allows nurses to stay inside the office all day long
options.B: It builds local ownership and trust in health programs
options.C: It forces community members to pay taxes to the clinic
options.D: It removes the need for professional nursing training

explanation: When residents participate in the diagnostic process, they value the resulting health interventions and support them willingly. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h4)

question: What role does the community health nurse play during participatory community diagnosis?

options.A: A politician who promises free money for everyone
options.B: A facilitator who guides and works alongside the community
options.C: A distant observer who never talks to local residents
options.D: A strict commander who gives orders without explanation

explanation: Nurses work collaboratively with local people to empower them rather than imposing solutions from above. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h4)

question: Why do policymakers need data gathered from a community diagnosis?

options.A: To prove that no diseases exist in rural areas
options.B: To increase the workload of community health nurses
options.C: To create policies based on actual local facts rather than guesses
options.D: To find reasons to close down poorly performing village clinics

explanation: Evidence-based planning ensures that health policies directly address proven local realities rather than assumptions. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h5)

question: What happens when health programs are copied from other regions without a local diagnosis?

options.A: They become cheaper for the local government to maintain
options.B: They automatically succeed because health problems are identical everywhere
options.C: They eliminate all infectious diseases within a single month
options.D: They may fail because they do not fit the local culture or environment

explanation: Every community is unique; interventions that work in one setting can easily fail if applied blindly elsewhere without local data. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h5)

question: Why is a community diagnosis considered an ongoing cycle rather than a single event?

options.A: Because government funding stops after the first month
options.B: Because health needs change and progress must be evaluated
options.C: Because nurses are required to rewrite reports every week
options.D: Because community members refuse to answer questions twice

explanation: Communities change over time, and nurses must continuously evaluate whether interventions are working and what new problems have arisen. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h6)

question: How does evaluation help ensure the sustainability of a health project?

options.A: It allows the government to stop sending free medical supplies
options.B: It proves that nurses no longer need to visit the village
options.C: It forces community leaders to take full financial blame for failures
options.D: It proves to the community that their hard work is producing results

explanation: Seeing tangible improvements encourages the community to keep up their healthy behaviors for the long term. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h6)
